summary: Anthony Franco of MLB Trade Rumors ranks the top 25 trade candidates of the 2023-24 MLB offseason, balancing trade value against likelihood of a move. Few teams are clearly rebuilding, so the list centers on stars deep into arbitration, such as Juan Soto, Corbin Burnes and Shane Bieber. Several clubs, including the Padres, Twins and Rays, are cutting payroll. The note gives salary projections, stats and front-office comments for each player, plus a list of other names of note.
one_line: MLB Trade Rumors ranks the 25 likeliest and most valuable 2023-24 offseason trade candidates, led by Juan Soto, Corbin Burnes and Willy Adames.
key_facts: Juan Soto is projected for a $33M arbitration salary, the highest ever for an arbitration-eligible player, and has one year of club control left; he hit .275/.410/.519 with 35 home runs in 2023.
The Padres are scaling back payroll, perhaps by as much as $50M, and need multiple starting pitchers.
Soto rejected a $440M offer from the Nationals before being traded at the 2022 deadline.
Corbin Burnes (projected $15.1M) and Willy Adames (projected $12.4M) are each one year from free agency; Burnes had a 3.39 ERA over 193 2/3 innings in 2023.
Shane Bieber is projected at $12.2M and one year from free agency; he had a 3.80 ERA over 21 starts and lost part of the second half to elbow inflammation.
Tyler Glasnow will make $25M in 2024, the largest single-year salary in Rays history, after a 3.53 ERA over 21 starts in 2023.
Dylan Cease had a 4.58 ERA over 177 innings in 2023 after a 2.20 mark the year before; he is two seasons from free agency and projected for $8.8M.
The White Sox lost 101 games; GM Chris Getz called Luis Robert Jr. a franchise building block after Robert hit 38 home runs with a .264/.315/.542 line.
Robert will make $12.5M in 2024 and $15M in 2025, with $20M team options for 2026-27.
Minnesota president Derek Falvey confirmed payroll is being pared back, possibly to $125M-140M from about $120M projected spending; Christian Vázquez has a three-year, $30M deal.
Alek Manoah had a 5.87 ERA over 19 outings in 2023; GM Ross Atkins said he would get 'a strong leg up' on the No. 5 rotation spot.
Pete Alonso is projected for a $22M arbitration salary, and Mets president David Stearns has twice said he expects Alonso to be the Opening Day first baseman.
The Tigers acquired Mark Canha from Milwaukee in the biggest trade of the offseason's first couple weeks.
